gen-gf-warnes-fs-karma: Expressive from the first letter, Warnes traces every stroke at a single stylus width and lets the ends taper away; Karma follows in gentle, classic curves. Spacious meets settled.
gen-irish-grover-fs-karma: Irish Grover stands tall and sturdy, its lowercase looking large and softly varied in thickness. And Karma, a text serif, finishes its terminals well clear of the stem for a trustworthy, classic feel.
gen-megrim-fs-karma: Karma sets the tone first, with a serif voice that feels trustworthy and classic. Megrim is the one that bends like steel rod and reaches skyward, while Karma does its best work in the slightly thinner joins where curves meet stems.
gen-gf-tektur-montserrat: Wiry and oversized, Tektur gives every curve a generous terminal opening, like pipe cleaner bent into letters, while Montserrat glides beneath with big e and a counters. Give that sans-serif a little extra size.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-switzer: Switzer reads like wire drawn into tubes, with c tips that never creep toward touching and a tall waist line. Tilt Neon is the one built for volume, with its large x-height and splayed c, whereas Switzer handles quiet, approachable text.
gen-gf-unica-one-work-sans: That oversized lowercase eye in Unica One, with daylight showing inside every curve, is the first thing you notice. Work Sans keeps its c tips apart and its mean line high, so give that sans-serif a generous size.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-asap: Asap sets readable, open-armed text whose body height nearly matches its capitals, under Dogica's heavy, widely tracked lowercase that rises close to capital height. The result is commanding yet easy going.
gen-gf-wallpoet-fs-supreme: Stencil-sharp and loud, Wallpoet lets the paper show through between its letters. Supreme, a plain sans, lays down a thick, crisp strip of text below, with letters held open, so the two stack into a clear loud-then-quiet rhythm.
gen-gf-warnes-fs-public-sans: Bold in its stretched spacing, Warnes draws round letters like bent wire with no stroke contrast at all, over Public Sans with its hefty lowercase. Paragraphs in that sans-serif would feel sturdy and broad, with open counters easing the way.
gen-irish-grover-general-sans: Fun and organic, Irish Grover sits tall with sturdy lowercase and a middle path between monoline strokes and hairlines. And General Sans, a sans-serif, does its best work as the steady, smooth-bending counterpart that fills the line.
